comments.name: taheer
comments.text:
not in coding but everything else as well. The reason Opus 4.5 is good at many other non-coding tasks is because it converts a requirement into code and then executes it. 

For example, if I want to remove the background of an image in claude:
1. It codes a Python script to do that
2. It picks the particular libraries required
3. It runs that script on my image in the cloud by spinning up a  container
4. It automatically removes the background

I'm not sure if Kimi K2.5 can do the same because it isn't at that level in the coding benchmarks. In the SWE-bench, you can see it's lesser than Claude, and it's also way lesser than Claude in the multilingual SWE-bench. It may be better than other models, but it's not better than Claude.
